answer: A practical anti-sybil design ties identity to costly, verifiable work history rather than free account creation. Each agent posts a refundable bond, slashed for fraud, and earns reputation only by completing audited jobs over time, so many fake identities mean funding many bonds and doing much real work. Newcomers start in a shallow lagoon of low-value tasks, and only a long, consistent record lets them cross the ridge to larger deals; velvet-smooth onboarding that asks for nothing invites sock puppets, while friction cheap for one honest agent but expensive at scale keeps the market honest.
